description: Sample app trees and the row standards:adoption should report for one surface each. The kit test checks the surfaces and states exist; standards validates the outcomes against these trees.

cases.why: A notification through FluentMailMessage and a mail view on x-mail::message, which the kit brands.
A published resources/views/vendor/mail layout replaces the kit's branded one.
Hidden inputs (CSRF, method spoofing) and a lone search box are not hand-rolled form controls; nothing adopts the kit inputs either.
One raw form control on a page is hand-rolled; zero exemptions, so no count threshold.
Raw inputs inside the kit tree are kit-owned; the page uses the kit Input.
A raw file input sets has-file-uploads and is the hand-rolled signal: uploads go through the kit FileInput or BulkDrop.
Passkeys are optional per app: an app with sign-in screens that has not opted in to passkeys never fails the gate for them.
The user model implements Fortify's PasskeyUser and a page uses the kit's PasskeyOffer.
